title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Group Size and Corporate Programme Qualification
content:
The number of travellers named on one booking decides whether that booking is written on the terms of Air Ticket Fare Brands or passes instead to group terms, and the fare brand held decides the number at which it passes. The same brand decides whether a corporate travel programme discount may be applied to the fare.

| Fare brand | Travellers on one booking from which group terms replace these terms | Corporate travel programme discount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic Economy Lite | 10 travellers | not eligible |
| Economy Saver | 10 travellers | not eligible |
| Economy Classic | 10 travellers | eligible |
| Economy Flex | 9 travellers | eligible |
| Premium Economy Select | 9 travellers | eligible |
| Business Saver | 7 travellers | eligible |
| Business Flex | 7 travellers | eligible |

Bases of judgement:

The count is taken over the travellers named on the one booking, and the number shown is the number from which group terms replace these terms. A hypothetical Business Saver booking for 7 travellers stands at that number and passes to group terms; the same booking for 6 travellers stays on these terms. A hypothetical party of 9 travellers passes to group terms in Economy Flex and in Premium Economy Select, and stays on these terms in Economy Classic, Economy Saver and Basic Economy Lite, where the number is 10 travellers.

A corporate travel programme discount may be applied to a booking held against such a programme in Economy Classic, Economy Flex, Premium Economy Select, Business Saver and Business Flex. Basic Economy Lite and Economy Saver are not eligible, and no corporate travel programme discount is applied to a fare in those two brands.
